mainTopic: Wonder stories of the sea, the לויתן and בהמות, the שר של ים, the ירדן, and the seas and rivers around ארץ ישראל
overview: This amud is full of אגדה about wonders of the sea and the desert. First the story of the jeweled crate ends: a בת קול says it belongs to the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and will hold תכלת for the צדיקים in עולם הבא. Then come more travelers' tales: a precious stone that brings the dead back to life, the shining eyes of the לויתן seen by רבי יהושע, and meat in the desert that healed itself on special grass. Next the גמרא explains the 'great sea monsters' of בראשית. רבי יוחנן says they are the two לויתנים, and רב teaches that the לויתן and the בהמות were made male and female and were stopped from having young so they would not destroy the world. The גמרא asks why the two females were treated differently and answers each question. רב also teaches that the שר של ים, named רהב, was killed at creation, and that the ירדן flows from the cave of Pamyas all the way to the לויתן's mouth. רבא בר עולא rereads a פסוק in איוב about this. Finally רב דימי brings teachings from ארץ ישראל: the seven seas and four rivers around ארץ ישראל, and the start of a teaching about what גבריאל will do in the future, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The diver and the angry fish
steps.stepSummary: The story of the jeweled crate continues: a diver goes down for the crate, the fish attack him, and he drives them off with vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: A diver went down to bring up the crate. The fish got angry and tried to tear off his thigh, but he threw a flask of vinegar at them and they swam down and away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up in the middle of a story from earlier on the daf about a crate full of jewels guarded by fish. A diver tries to grab it and fights off the fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step is the action part of the story. It sets up the surprise ending in the next step, where a heavenly voice tells them the crate is not theirs to take.

phrases.english: a diver [went down] to bring it up,
phrases.notes: The words 'went down' come right before this, on the previous amud. 'It' is the jeweled crate.

phrases.english: and [the fish] got angry and wanted to tear off his thigh,
and he threw a flask of vinegar, and they went down.
phrases.notes: The fish sank back down and left him alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the crate story begun before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The diver drives off the guarding fish with vinegar.

steps.title: A heavenly voice: the crate belongs to רבי חנינא בן דוסא's wife
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול tells them to leave the crate alone, because it belongs to the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and will hold תכלת for the צדיקים in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said to us: 'What business do you have with the crate of the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא? She is going to put תכלת in it for the righteous in the World to Come!'
steps.whatsHappening: The crate story ends: a voice from heaven says the treasure is set aside for the wife of the great צדיק רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending changes how we see the treasure. It is not lost loot for whoever finds it. It is a reward stored away for a צדיק's family, to be used for a מצוה (תכלת for ציצית) in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת, the sky-blue wool used for ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: The jeweled crate is set aside in heaven's plan for the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא, to hold תכלת for the צדיקים in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to us:
"What business do you have with

phrases.aramaic: קַרְטְלִיתָא דִּדְבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא,
phrases.english: the crate of the wife of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
who is destined to put sky-blue wool in it
for the righteous in the World to Come!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ending and meaning of the crate story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crate is reserved for the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא, for תכלת for the צדיקים in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רב יהודה הינדוא sees a stone guarded by a snake
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: on a ship, they see a precious stone with a snake wrapped around it. When a diver goes for it, the snake tries to swallow the ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה from India tells: Once we were traveling on a ship and saw a precious stone with a snake coiled around it. A diver went down to bring it up, and the snake came and tried to swallow the ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new wonder story, told by רב יהודה הינדוא. This step sets the scene and the danger for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the crate story, a treasure in the sea is guarded by a creature, and a diver tries to get it. Here the guard is huge and dangerous enough to threaten the whole ship.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda the Indian relates:
Once we were traveling on a ship,
and we saw a certain precious stone
that a snake was coiled around.
A diver went down to bring it up,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא תַּנִּינָא קָא בָּעֵי לְמִבְלַע לַהּ לִסְפִינְתָּא.
phrases.english: and the snake came, wanting to swallow the ship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story in the same chain of sea wonders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A snake guarding a precious stone threatens to swallow the ship.

steps.title: The snake is killed and brought back to life by the stone
steps.stepSummary: A raven cuts off the snake's head and the sea turns to blood. Then another snake hangs the precious stone on it, the dead snake comes back to life, and it attacks the ship again.
steps.simpleTranslation: A raven came and cut off its head, and the water turned into blood. Another snake came, took the stone, hung it on the dead snake, and it came back to life. It came again, trying to swallow the ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going: the snake is killed, and then the precious stone brings it back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step reveals the stone's power: it can revive the dead. That explains why the snake guarded it, and it sets up the second attack.

keyTerms.meaning: its fellow, another one like it
and it came back to life

phrases.english: A raven came and cut off its head,
the water turned and became blood.
Its fellow snake came,
took it, hung it on him, and he came back to life.
phrases.notes: The second snake took the precious stone and hung it on the dead snake.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אֲתָא קָא בָּעֵי בָּלְעָא לִסְפִינְתָּא,
phrases.english: It came again, wanting to swallow the ship,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the snake story and shows the stone's power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The precious stone brings the dead snake back to life.

steps.title: The stone lands on the ship and the salted birds fly away with it
steps.stepSummary: A bird kills the snake again and throws the stone onto the ship. The travelers place it on salted birds, which come back to life and fly off with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again a bird came and cut off its head. It took that precious stone and threw it onto the ship. We had some salted birds with us, and we put the stone on them. They took it and flew away with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the stone reaches the ship, and when the travelers test it on salted, dead birds, the birds revive and carry the stone away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending proves the stone's life-giving power a second time, now on birds that were already salted. Ironically, the stone's own power is what makes the travelers lose it.

phrases.english: Again a bird came and cut off its head.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁקְלוּהָ לְהַהִיא אֶבֶן טָבָא שַׁדְיוּהָ לִסְפִינְתָּא;
phrases.english: It took that precious stone and threw it onto the ship;
we had these salted birds with us,
we placed it on them;
they took it and flew away with it.
phrases.notes: The salted birds came back to life from the stone, then carried it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the snake story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stone even revives salted birds, which fly off with it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע trembles at a great light in the sea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: on a ship, רבי יהושע, who was awake, trembles. רבי אליעזר wakes up and asks why, and רבי יהושע says he saw a great light in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע were traveling on a ship. רבי אליעזר was sleeping and רבי יהושע was awake. רבי יהושע trembled, and רבי אליעזר woke up. He asked him, 'What is this, יהושע? Why did you tremble?' He answered, 'I saw a great light in the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about huge sea creatures. This step sets up the mystery of the light, which רבי אליעזר explains next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story comes from תנאים, not later travelers, and it leads into a פסוק about the לויתן. The question and answer here only describe what was seen. The explanation comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
who were traveling on a ship,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר יָשֵׁן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נֵעוֹר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer was sleeping and Rabbi Yehoshua was awake.

phrases.aramaic: נִזְדַּעְזַע רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְנִנְעַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua trembled, and Rabbi Eliezer woke up.
He said to him: What is this, Yehoshua?
Why did you tremble?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מָאוֹר גָּדוֹל רָאִיתִי בַּיָּם.
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw a great light in the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from travelers' tales to a ברייתא about the great sea creatures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע saw a great light in the sea.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: it was the eyes of the לויתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר suggests the light was the eyes of the לויתן and backs it up with a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Maybe you saw the eyes of the לויתן, as it is written: 'His eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains the mysterious light by pointing to a פסוק that describes the לויתן's eyes as shining like dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation ties a real sighting to a פסוק. Since the פסוק compares the לויתן's eyes to the first light of morning, a great light in the sea could be those eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: the Leviathan, the giant sea creature

steps.whatToRemember: The great light רבי יהושע saw is explained as the shining eyes of the לויתן, based on איוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא עֵינָיו שֶׁל לִוְיָתָן רָאִיתָ –
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps you saw the eyes of the Leviathan,
as it is written: "His eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn."
phrases.notes: איוב 41:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא עֵינָיו שֶׁל לִוְיָתָן רָאִיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the light described in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The light was the eyes of the לויתן, as the פסוק describes them shining like dawn.

steps.title: A thigh of meat heals itself on the desert grass
steps.stepSummary: הונא בר נתן tells רב אשי that in the desert they cut open a thigh of meat, removed the forbidden parts, and laid it on grass. By the time they brought wood, the meat had healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: הונא בר נתן told me: Once we were traveling in the desert, and we had a thigh of meat with us. We cut it open, removed the forbidden parts, and put it on the grass. By the time we brought wood, the thigh had healed, and we roasted it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new wonder story begins, this time on land in the desert. Meat that was cut open heals itself after lying on some grass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setting moves from sea to desert, but the theme stays amazing natural wonders. Why the meat healed is explained by אמימר in step 10.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Huna bar Natan told me:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָא אָזְלִינַן בְּמַדְבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Once we were traveling in the desert,
and we had a thigh of meat with us.
We cut it open, removed [the forbidden parts], and put it on the grass.
By the time we brought wood,
the thigh had healed, and we roasted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new wonder story, now set in the desert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat placed on a certain grass healed itself.

steps.title: The coals still glow a year later
steps.stepSummary: Coming back twelve months later, they find the coals from their fire still glowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we came back after twelve months of the year, we saw those coals still glowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The story adds a second wonder: the coals from the fire they cooked on were still burning a full year later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two mysteries, the healing grass and the long-burning coals. This step sets up the explanation that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲדַרַן לְבָתַר תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא,
phrases.english: When we returned after twelve months of the year,
we saw those coals
that were still glowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲדַרַן לְבָתַר תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second wonder to the desert story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The coals were still glowing after a year.

steps.title: אמימר explains: healing grass and broom coals
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains both wonders: the grass was a healing herb (סמתרי), and the coals were from broom wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came before אמימר, he said to me: That grass was a life-giving herb, and those coals were from broom wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The narrator comes before אמימר, and אמימר gives a natural explanation for each wonder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both mysteries are solved by what the things were made of. The grass had healing power, which is why the meat closed up. The coals were broom wood, which is why they burned so long.
steps.whatToRemember: Both desert wonders have explanations: the grass was a healing herb, and the coals came from broom wood.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַמֵּימָר, אֲמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I came before Ameimar, he said to me:
That grass was a life-giving herb;
those coals were of broom wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַמֵּימָר, אֲמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two wonders from steps 8 and 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grass was סמתרי, a healing herb, and the coals were from broom wood.

steps.title: The great sea monsters: the Babylonian reading
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ויברא אלהים את התנינים הגדולים' is explained in בבל as sea oryxes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And God created the great sea monsters.' Here in בבל they translated it as 'sea oryxes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the great sea creatures and gives the first explanation of who they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps going with the theme of huge sea creatures from the earlier stories. The first view says the תנינים are a kind of large sea animal named after a land animal. It sets up רבי יוחנן's different view in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Sea monsters, very large sea creatures
Sea oryxes, a kind of large sea creature

phrases.english: "And God created the great sea monsters"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:21

phrases.english: Here they translated it:
phrases.notes: "Here" means in בבל, where the גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: sea oryxes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories of wonders in the sea and desert to explaining a פסוק about the great sea creatures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל, the תנינים הגדולים were explained as sea oryxes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the sea monsters are the לויתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the תנינים are the two לויתנים from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: This means the לויתן the straight serpent and the לויתן the twisting serpent. As the פסוק says: 'On that day God will punish with His hard sword,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different explanation of the same פסוק. He says the 'great sea monsters' are the two לויתנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the plural 'תנינים' in בראשית as the two לויתנים that ישעיהו 27:1 names: the straight serpent and the twisting serpent. This opens the way for רב's teaching about a male and a female לויתן.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on: the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
This is the leviathan, the straight serpent
and the leviathan, the twisting serpent,
as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִפְקֹד ה׳ בְּחַרְבּוֹ הַקָּשָׁה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "On that day God will punish with His hard sword, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:1. The rest of the פסוק names both לויתנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנינים הגדולים are the two לויתנים: the straight serpent and the twisting serpent.

steps.title: Everything was made male and female, including the לויתן
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the לויתן was made male and female. To protect the world, הקדוש ברוך הוא castrated the male and killed and salted the female for the צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: Everything, time, ירדן.) רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Everything הקדוש ברוך הוא created in His world, He created male and female. Even the straight serpent לויתן and the twisting serpent לויתן were created male and female. If they had mated, they would have destroyed the whole world. What did הקדוש ברוך הוא do? He castrated the male, and He killed the female and salted her for the צדיקים in the future. As the פסוק says: 'And He will kill the sea monster that is in the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב teaches that the two לויתנים are a male and a female. God made sure they could not have young, and He saved the female as food for the צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on רבי יוחנן: the two לויתנים are a pair. Their young would have wrecked the world, so God castrated the male and killed the female. The פסוק 'והרג את התנין' is the source for killing her.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember a list of teachings
In the future world to come

phrases.english: (Memory sign: Everything, time, Jordan)
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: Read it as "רב יהודה אמר רב." The colon after the first word is just in the wrong place.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ –
phrases.english: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world
He created them male and female.
Even the leviathan, the straight serpent,
and the leviathan, the twisting serpent:
He created them male and female,
and if they had mated with each other,
they would destroy the entire world.
What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do?
He castrated the male,
and killed the female
and salted her for the righteous in the future to come,
as it is stated: "And He will kill the sea monster that is in the sea."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's two לויתנים, explaining them as a male and a female.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לויתן pair was male and female. The male was castrated, and the female was killed and salted for the צדיקים.

steps.title: The giant land beasts were also male and female
steps.stepSummary: The same is true of the בהמות בהררי אלף. Here God castrated the male and cooled the female, saving her for the צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also the beasts on a thousand hills were created male and female. If they had mated, they would have destroyed the whole world. What did הקדוש ברוך הוא do? He castrated the male, cooled the female, and kept her for the צדיקים in the future. As the פסוק says: 'Behold now, his strength is in his loins.' That is the male. 'And his power is in the muscles of his belly.' That is the female.
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues with the giant land animals. The plan is similar, but the female is cooled and kept alive, not killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The male is castrated just like the לויתן. But the female בהמות is not killed. Instead, her desire is cooled. This difference sets up the questions in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The giant beasts on a thousand hills
He cooled, meaning He took away her desire

phrases.english: And even the beasts on a thousand hills:
phrases.notes: The phrase comes from תהלים 50:10. These are huge land animals.

phrases.english: He created them male and female,
and if they had mated with each other,
they would destroy the entire world.
What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do?
He castrated the male,
and cooled the female,
and kept her for the righteous in the future to come,
as it is stated: "Behold now, his strength is in his loins":
phrases.notes: איוב 40:16

phrases.english: this is the male,
"and his power is in the muscles of his belly":
this is the female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב's rule to a second giant creature, with a different way of handling the female.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The male בהמות was castrated, and the female was cooled and kept for the צדיקים.

steps.title: Why not just cool the female לויתן too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why God did not handle the לויתן the same way as the בהמות: castrate the male and cool the female.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, by the לויתן, let Him castrate the male and cool the female!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the different treatment. If cooling worked for the female בהמות, why kill the female לויתן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question compares the two cases. Cooling looks gentler and enough, so killing the female לויתן seems unneeded.

phrases.english: There too,
phrases.notes: "There" means the לויתן.

phrases.english: let Him castrate the male
and cool the female!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why steps 13 and 14 handle the two females differently.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cooling was enough for the בהמות, so it should have been enough for the לויתן.

steps.title: Fish are unrestrained
steps.stepSummary: Cooling would not work for fish, because fish are too wild in mating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fish are unrestrained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that cooling would not stop a fish. So the female לויתן had to be killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish are wild by nature, so even a cooled female would still have young. Killing her was the only safe way.

phrases.english: Fish are unrestrained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a difference in nature between fish and land animals
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cooling would work for the לויתן just as for the בהמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fish are too wild for cooling to work, so the female had to be killed.

steps.title: Then why not kill the male instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why God did not do the opposite and kill and salt the male לויתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let Him do the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If one לויתן had to be killed, why the female and not the male?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the male is castrated anyway, it seems it would work just as well to kill and salt him. The question asks why the female was chosen.

phrases.english: Then let Him do the opposite!
phrases.notes: Kill and salt the male instead of the female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that one לויתן had to be killed, but asks why it was the female.
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing the female לויתן to be killed and salted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Killing the male would also stop them from having young.

steps.title: Two reasons the female was chosen
steps.stepSummary: First answer: a salted female tastes better. Second answer: the male is kept for God to 'play with,' and this is not fitting with a female.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: a salted female is better. If you want, say: since it is written, 'This לויתן You formed to play with,' it is not proper to do this with a female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers for why the female was killed and the male kept alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is about taste: a salted female makes a better meal for the צדיקים. The second answer comes from a פסוק in תהלים: the לויתן is kept for God's 'play,' and it is only fitting for that to be the male.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: this introduces one possible answer

phrases.english: If you want, say:
a salted female is better;
if you want, say:
since it is written:
"This leviathan You formed to play with,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:26

phrases.english: with a female it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with two separate reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate reasons: one about taste, one from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It makes no difference which לויתן is killed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The female is killed either because she tastes better salted, or because the male must stay alive for God's 'play.'

steps.title: Why not salt the female בהמות too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the female בהמות was cooled and not killed and salted like the לויתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, by the בהמות, let Him salt the female!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the question the other way around. If salting works so well, why not salt the female בהמות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said a salted female makes a fine meal. So it seems the female בהמות could also have been killed and salted, not just cooled.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the בהמות.

phrases.english: let Him salt the female!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the comparison around and questions the treatment of the בהמות.
steps.kashyaTarget: Cooling the female בהמות instead of salting her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If salting the female works for the לויתן, it should work for the בהמות too.

steps.title: Salted fish is good, salted meat is not
steps.stepSummary: Salting suits fish but not meat, so the female בהמות was kept alive and cooled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Salted fish is good. Salted meat is not good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that salting only works well for fish. That is why the land animal was kept fresh by cooling instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לויתן is a fish, so salting keeps it tasty. The בהמות is a land animal, and salted meat is not good, so God kept her alive. This finishes the comparison between the two giant creatures.
steps.whatToRemember: Both giant pairs, the לויתן and the בהמות, were stopped from having young so they would not destroy the world, and both are saved for the צדיקים. The differences come from their nature. Fish are too wild for cooling, so the female לויתן was killed and salted. Salted meat is not good, so the female בהמות was cooled and kept alive.

phrases.english: Salted fish is good,
salted meat is not good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 and closes the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a difference between fish and meat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salting would work equally well for the בהמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fish is good salted, so the female בהמות was cooled and kept alive.

steps.title: The Minister of the Sea Refuses and Is Killed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: at creation, הקדוש ברוך הוא told the שר של ים to swallow all the waters. He refused, so God struck him and killed him, as the פסוק in איוב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When God wanted to create the world, He told the angel in charge of the sea, 'Open your mouth and swallow all the water in the world.' The angel answered, 'Master of the world, it is enough for me to stay with my own water.' Right away God kicked him and killed him, as the verse says: 'With His power He stirs up the sea, and by His understanding He smites רהב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יהודה in the name of רב. It tells a story about creation and the angel in charge of the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God wanted the waters swallowed so that dry land could appear. The שר של ים refused and wanted to keep only his own waters, so God killed him. The פסוק from איוב is brought as the source, because it speaks of God striking the sea and 'רהב'.

keyTerms.meaning: The minister (angel) in charge of the sea

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to create the world,
He said to the minister of the sea:

phrases.aramaic: פְּתַח פִּיךָ וּבְלַע כׇּל מֵימוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Open your mouth and swallow all the waters in the world.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
it is enough that I stay with my own.
Immediately He kicked him and killed him,
as it is stated: "With His power He stirs up the sea,
and by His understanding He smites Rahab."
phrases.notes: איוב 26:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the לויתן and בהמות discussion to another רב teaching about the sea at creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At creation the שר של ים refused God's command to swallow the waters and was killed, as shown by איוב 26:12.

steps.title: The Minister of the Sea Is Named Rahab, and the Water Hides His Smell
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from that פסוק that the שר של ים is named רהב. He adds that his dead body would smell unbearable if the sea did not cover it, and reads a פסוק in ישעיהו as a hint to this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Learn from here that the name of the sea's angel is רהב. If the water did not cover him, no creature could stand his smell. As the verse says: 'They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain, as the waters cover the sea.' Don't read it as 'cover the sea'; read it as 'cover the angel of the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק builds on the story just told. He draws two new ideas: the angel's name, and the reason he is hidden under the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק said God 'smites רהב' in the same breath as the sea, רבי יצחק concludes that רהב is the name of the שר של ים. He then reads 'the waters cover the sea' in ישעיהו as 'the waters cover the angel of the sea', which explains why his smell does not reach us.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
Rahab, the name of the minister of the sea
Do not read it as; a way of reading a פסוק with a different meaning

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the words of the פסוק. It is a way of finding an extra hidden meaning, while the plain meaning stays.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: Learn from this
that the minister of the sea's name is "Rahab";
and were it not that water covers him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the angel God killed in the last step, so this is about his dead body.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כׇּל בְּרִיָּה יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּרֵיחוֹ,
phrases.english: no creature could stand his smell,
as it is stated: "They shall not hurt nor destroy
in all My holy mountain, etc.,
as the waters cover the sea."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 11:9

phrases.english: Do not read it as "cover the sea,"
but rather "cover the minister of the sea."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws new conclusions from the פסוק and the story in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שר של ים is named רהב, and the sea covers his body so that his smell does not harm the world.

steps.title: The Jordan Starts at the Cave of Pamyas
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב that the ירדן river comes out of the cave of Pamyas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The ירדן comes out of the cave of Pamyas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another short teaching from רב יהודה in the name of רב, this time about where the ירדן begins. It sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple statement of fact about the source of the ירדן. It leads into a longer ברייתא that agrees with it and follows the river all the way to the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: The cave of Pamyas, in the far north of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The Jordan comes out of the cave of Pamyas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from the same pair, רב יהודה in the name of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ירדן begins at the cave of Pamyas.

steps.title: A ברייתא Agrees and Follows the Jordan to the Leviathan
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says the ירדן comes out of the cave of Pamyas. It adds that the river flows through two lakes, down to the Great Sea, and on to the mouth of the לויתן, quoting a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: The ירדן comes out of the cave of Pamyas. It flows through the Sea of Sivchi and the Sea of טבריא, and rolls down into the Great Sea. It keeps rolling down until it reaches the mouth of the לויתן, as the verse says: 'He is confident, though the ירדן rushes into his mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says the same thing as רב, which supports his teaching. The ברייתא then traces the rest of the river's path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line of the ברייתא matches רב word for word, so it is support for him. The ברייתא adds the river's whole route and uses a פסוק from איוב to say it ends at the לויתן's mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
The Jordan comes out of the cave of Pamyas,
and travels through the Sea of Sivchi
and through the Sea of Tiberias,
and rolls down to the Great Sea;

phrases.aramaic: וּמִתְגַּלְגֵּל וְיוֹרֵד עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְפִיו שֶׁל לִוְיָתָן,
phrases.english: and rolls down until it reaches the mouth of the Leviathan,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יִבְטַח כִּי יָגִיחַ יַרְדֵּן אֶל פִּיהוּ״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "He is confident, though the Jordan rushes into his mouth."
phrases.notes: איוב 40:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's statement in step 23 with a ברייתא and adds more details.
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that the ירדן comes out of the cave of Pamyas.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same words and traces the river to the לויתן.

steps.title: רבא בר עולא: That Verse Is About the בהמות
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא challenges the ברייתא's use of the פסוק. The פסוק is written about the בהמות, not the לויתן, so 'his mouth' cannot mean the לויתן's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא objected: This verse is written about the בהמות on a thousand hills!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר עולא attacks the proof from the פסוק that the ברייתא just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read 'the ירדן rushes into his mouth' as the לויתן's mouth. But the פסוק appears in the section about the בהמות, the giant land animals. So the reading seems not to fit.

phrases.english: Rava bar Ulla strongly objected to this:
This is written about the Behemoth on a thousand hills!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסוק used at the end of the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of איוב 40:23 as the ירדן flowing into the לויתן's mouth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's context is the בהמות, so it cannot be describing the לויתן.

steps.title: רבא בר עולא's New Reading: The בהמות Feel Safe When the ירדן Reaches the לויתן
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא explains the פסוק in a way that fits both: the בהמות feel confident when the ירדן flows into the לויתן's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא בר עולא said: When are the בהמות on a thousand hills confident? When the ירדן rushes into the לויתן's mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר עולא answers his own challenge by giving a new meaning to the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stays about the בהמות: 'he is confident' refers to the בהמות. What makes them confident is that the ירדן flows into the לויתן's mouth. So the idea that the ירדן reaches the לויתן is kept, while the פסוק fits its context.
steps.whatToRemember: The ירדן flows from the cave of Pamyas to the Great Sea and into the לויתן's mouth. The פסוק in איוב is about the בהמות, who feel secure when that happens.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava bar Ulla said:
When are the Behemoth on a thousand hills confident?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמֵּגִיחַ יַרְדֵּן בְּפִיו שֶׁל לִוְיָתָן.
phrases.english: When the Jordan rushes into the mouth of the Leviathan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 25 with a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק so that it fits its context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק describes the לויתן being confident as the ירדן flows into his mouth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes the בהמות being confident, at the time the ירדן flows into the לויתן's mouth.

steps.title: רב דימי: Seven Seas and Four Rivers Surround ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign for the next teachings, רב דימי quotes רבי יוחנן explaining a פסוק in תהלים: the 'seas' and 'rivers' are seven seas and four rivers around ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: Seas, גבריאל, hungry.) When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the verse mean, 'For He founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers'? These are the seven seas and four rivers that surround ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives a memory sign for three teachings of רב דימי. Then it brings the first one, which explains a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the land resting on 'seas' and 'rivers'. רבי יוחנן says these words point to a specific set: seven seas and four rivers that surround ארץ ישראל. The next step will list them.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign listing the next teachings
When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: (Memory sign: Seas, Gabriel, hungry)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For He founded it upon the seas,
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:2

phrases.english: and established it upon the rivers"?
These are seven seas and four rivers
that surround the Land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new set of teachings from רב דימי, still on the theme of seas and rivers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'seas' and 'rivers' in תהלים 24:2 are seven seas and four rivers surrounding ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The List of the Seven Seas and Four Rivers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן names the seven seas and the four rivers that surround ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the seven seas: the Sea of טבריא, the Sea of סדום, the Sea of Cheilat, the Sea of Cheilata, the Sea of Sivchi, the Sea of Aspamya, and the Great Sea. And these are the four rivers: the ירדן, the Yarmuch, the Keiromyon, and the Pigah.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues by listing exactly which seas and rivers it means. Nothing is being argued here; it is a list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said there are seven seas and four rivers, and now each one is named. Some names are familiar, like the Sea of Tiberias (the Kinneret), the Sea of Sodom (the Dead Sea), and the ירדן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sea of Sodom (the Dead Sea)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, ארץ ישראל is surrounded by seven seas and four rivers, and this is the meaning of 'He founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers'.

phrases.english: And these are the seven seas:

phrases.aramaic: יַמָּהּ שֶׁל טְבֶרְיָא, וְיַמָּהּ שֶׁל סְדוֹם,
phrases.english: the Sea of Tiberias, and the Sea of Sodom,

phrases.aramaic: וְיַמָּהּ שֶׁל חֵילָת, וְיַמָּהּ שֶׁל חֵילָתָא,
phrases.english: and the Sea of Cheilat, and the Sea of Cheilata,
and the Sea of Sivchi, and the Sea of Aspamya,
and the Great Sea.
And these are the four rivers:
the Jordan, and the Yarmuch, and the Keiromyon, and the Pigah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the names of the seven seas and four rivers mentioned in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seven seas are Tiberias, Sodom, Cheilat, Cheilata, Sivchi, Aspamya, and the Great Sea; the four rivers are the ירדן, Yarmuch, Keiromyon, and Pigah.

steps.title: רבי יונתן begins a teaching about what גבריאל will do in the future
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a new statement from רבי יונתן: in the future, גבריאל will perform some action. What that action is comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי יונתן said: In the future, גבריאל will perform...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new teaching, and this line only sets it up. We learn who said it and that it is about something גבריאל will do in the future, but the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כי אתא tell us רב דימי was bringing a teaching from ארץ ישראל to בבל. The teaching belongs to רבי יונתן, and the word עתיד shows it describes the future. For now, just hold on to the question: what will גבריאל do?

keyTerms.meaning: When he came. This is used for a scholar arriving from ארץ ישראל to בבל with teachings.
The sage whose teaching רב דימי reports here.
In the future. This describes something that has not happened yet.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not try to work out what גבריאל will do from this line alone, because the next words tell us.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings with him.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yonatan says:
In the future, Gabriel will perform

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's list of the seas and rivers around ארץ ישראל in step 28, רב דימי brings another aggadic teaching, this time in the name of רבי יונתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the name of רבי יונתן: in the future, גבריאל will perform an action. The action is described on the next amud.
